correctness.rationale: For all integer n, the complete totient-six index set is {7,9,14,18}. Exact 12-by-12 Sylvester determinants are 2^6*29^2 (index 7) and 19^3*37 (index 9), so parity excludes all but three common primes. Exhaustive prime-field root lists (29:{23,24}, 19:{4,5,16}, 37:{33}) and distinct unique lifting digits prove all common valuations at most one, not merely for a finite n-range. Reflection handles indices 14,18. Disjoint local residue sets and CRT prove the product formula, frequencies, exact least period 20387 and sharp maximum. A standalone Python check replayed both determinants, all root/lift certificates, 20387 full-period direct samples and negative n checks. Infinite n coverage follows from algebraic proof, not finite test.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary results give cyclotomic index identities, fixed-base varying-exponent GCD bounds, and height theory, not the complete four-index neighboring-argument GCD law. Published related calculations treat degree-two and degree-four polynomials; their statements do not entail the exact degree-six formulas, prime-square exclusion and eight-value CRT distribution. Search and content inspection provide reasonable but non-exhaustive priority evidence.
residual_risks: An older unindexed or poorly searchable common-root table might already yield the complete degree-six GCD formulas and period distribution.
Not every potentially relevant abstract led to a readable complete primary article; lower-degree published records were compared only at statement/abstract level.
Scientific originality and priority have not been independently assessed.

value.rationale: The set of four sextic cyclotomic indices is a natural complete first layer beyond the low-degree family, with all integer arguments rather than an arbitrary cutoff. The finding classifies all local common factors and their prime-square obstructions, the exact four-way overlap and the sharp least-period frequency spectrum. The result exposes multiple local collisions not determined by general resultant bounds or previously studied degree-two/four neighboring-value distributions; a finite-degree but infinite-input structural classification is a meaningful exact invariant.
